source.title: People v Thompson (2016 NY Slip Op 00997)

captionLines: The People of the State of New York, Respondent,

qualifierLines: {**26 NY3d at 681} OPINION OF THE COURT

The instant robberies were committed on February 18 and February 25, 2010 and, in December 2010, Supreme Court sentenced defendant, as a second felony offender, to concurrent terms of 20 years' incarceration to be followed by five years' postrelease supervision (PRS) with respect to that conviction. Defendant was adjudicated a second felony offender based on a prior drug conviction.

Supreme Court agreed with the People that the date of the resentence, not the date of the original sentence, is the controlling date for the calculation of the look-back period, and it adjudicated defendant a second violent felony offender for the purpose of imposing sentence upon the instant conviction. In resentencing defendant with respect to those robbery crimes, the court reimposed its initial punishment, that is, it ordered concurrent determinate terms of 20 years' incarceration to be followed by five years' PRS.
